chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yazid ibn Khalifa, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) advised us, commanded [good], and encouraged asceticism. Then he said: 'Upon you is devoutness (al-wara'), for whatever is with Allah cannot be attained except through devoutness.'

key_terms.الْوَرَعِ: Devoutness, piety, caution in religious matters

ai.seo_question: What is the key to attaining what is with Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies 'al-wara'' (spiritual caution) not merely as a virtue but as the indispensable key to attaining divine proximity and rewards. This emphasis aligns with the Shia scholarly tradition, which views wara' as the safeguard of faith against subtle sins, ensuring that one's deeds are accepted and not invalidated by doubtful matters.
